title: Mobile education builds resilience during shocks in five countries.

honest_claim_h3: No claim possible: no data is available. If released, a model could at most predict which children in these five randomized trials gained most from phone tutoring (heterogeneous treatment effects).

plain_idea.one_liner: Use child and household survey answers to predict which children benefit most from phone-call math tutoring during school closures.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-child baseline survey answers and treatment assignment from five randomized trials; about 7,800+ children per the paper's caption, count unverified because no files exist.
plain_idea.predict: The child's end-of-trial numeracy level (0-4 scale from a phone-administered assessment), or the individual gain from tutoring versus control.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Education NGOs and governments could target tutoring to the children who gain most, but the topic is education economics, outside this project's biology scope.

ml_idea: Heterogeneous-treatment-effect modelling (e.g. causal forests) on pooled multi-country trial microdata to find which children gain most from phone tutoring, testing transfer by holding out a whole country. Not feasible: the data repository is empty, and the topic is not biology.
